regulator.document: Amateur Radio Wireless Telegraphy Licence Conditions Booklet OFW611 (published 21 February 2024), Schedule 1 Tables A/B/C

note: Ofcom issues a single licence in three classes - Foundation, Intermediate and Full - each with its own frequency/power table in Schedule 1 of licence booklet OFW611 (published 21 February 2024; the 2024 reform, announced/rolled out Feb-Apr 2024, gave Foundation and Intermediate access to nearly all bands previously Full-only). Peak envelope power limits: Foundation 25 W, Intermediate 100 W, Full 1000 W on primary allocations and 400 W on secondary allocations; band-specific caps override class caps (160m above 1850 kHz 32 W, 6m above 51 MHz 100 W, 4m 160 W, 70cm 430-432 MHz 40 W ERP, 630m 5 W EIRP, 2200m 1 W ERP, Foundation on 10 GHz 1 W, Foundation on 2.4/5.7 GHz bands 2 W). Band privileges differ as follows: 630m (472-479 kHz) and the channelised 60m band (5258.5-5406.5 kHz, 11 discrete channels, 100 W PEP but not exceeding 200 W EIRP, licence note G conditions) are Full-only; Foundation additionally lacks 23cm (1240-1325 MHz) and the 2.3 GHz/3.4 GHz/5.83-5.85 GHz segments. All three classes share 2200m, 160m-10m, 6m, 4m, 2m and 70cm. The licence imposes no mode restrictions, only power/status limits; geographic or coordination conditions exist on 70cm (431-432 MHz excluded within 100 km of Charing Cross, London), 10m (within 50 km of Waddington) and 2m (within 50 km of Scarborough). Airborne operation is limited to 500 mW EIRP where stated. The 4m band is 70.0-70.5 MHz (69.9-70.5 is not a UK allocation; 70.5-71.5 MHz is a separate Full-only NoV 'innovation band'). NoV-only Full bands 146-147 MHz, 2300-2302 MHz and >275 GHz are excluded here.
